title: Hands and a library
brief: The agent needs tools, knowledge and sometimes other agents. Where each one lives decides who holds the credentials, who versions the definition and where the tokens are spent.

blocks.md:
A **Toolbox** groups tools behind one managed MCP-compatible endpoint with central auth (Microsoft Entra, OAuth identity passthrough), toolbox-level guardrails and versioning [[r3]]. You create a version, test it, promote it to default and consuming agents pick it up with no redeploy. Any MCP client can consume it. Agent Framework hosted agents use `FoundryToolbox` in Python or `AddFoundryToolboxes` in .NET.

Tool authentication can be key based, Microsoft Entra (agent identity or project managed identity), OAuth identity passthrough (on-behalf-of) or unauthenticated where that is appropriate [[r1]]. These options also apply to remote MCP servers.

blocks.title: How a tool reaches the agent
blocks.intro: Toolboxes are GA as of 2026-10-13. Tool search and skills inside them are preview.

options.name: Toolbox endpoint
options.summary: Many tools behind one managed MCP-compatible endpoint with central auth, guardrails and versions.
pros: Versioned promotion with no consumer redeploy
Non-Foundry MCP clients can consume it
cons: Some tools are not toolbox eligible
A promoted default reaches every consumer at once
options.bestWhen: Several agents share tools and you want central versioning.
options.avoidWhen: One agent uses one tool and nothing is shared.

options.name: Direct tool integration
options.summary: Attach a built-in tool straight to the agent.
pros: The only route for computer use, SharePoint, image generation, Azure Functions, Grounding with Bing and Fabric data agent
cons: Credentials and guardrails live per agent
options.bestWhen: The tool is not toolbox eligible.
options.avoidWhen: Many agents repeat the same wiring.

options.name: Client-side function calling
options.summary: The model asks, your process runs the function.
pros: Execution and data stay in your process
cons: You own the loop and retries
The agent optimizer cannot evaluate tool execution because it runs client side
options.bestWhen: Execution must stay inside your own trust boundary.
options.avoidWhen: The tool is a shared, governed capability.

options.name: Plain remote MCP server
options.summary: Point an agent at an MCP server and pick an auth option.
pros: Key, Entra or OAuth passthrough auth
options.bestWhen: One agent needs one external MCP server.
options.avoidWhen: You want a governed catalog with versions.

blocks.title: Tool paths into one agent
blocks.alt: The agent reaches a toolbox MCP endpoint that fronts an MCP server, Azure AI Search, OpenAPI and an A2A peer. It also calls functions in its own process and attaches direct tools.

blocks.title: Foundry IQ or something else
blocks.prompt: Change what the content is, who may see it and how much control you need.

values.label: Documents a user uploads in chat

options.name: Azure AI Search tool
options.summary: Your own index behind a tool.

org.why: Sources include Blob Storage, SharePoint, OneLake and the public web.

user.why: Built for curated content, not per-chat uploads.

open.why: Works, but ACL sync is wasted.

acl.why: Syncs ACLs for supported sources, honors Purview labels and can run as the caller.

managed.why: Agentic retrieval with minimal, low or medium effort.

custom.why: Fewer knobs than your own pipeline.

org.why: Good when you already own the index.

user.why: An index per chat upload is heavy.

acl.why: You design the security filters yourself.

org.why: Not aimed at large curated corpora.

user.why: The docs point here for user documents.

open.why: Fine for content the user brought.

acl.why: Enforce any rule at query time.

org.why: Per-user and LLM-consolidated, wrong for shared policy documents (inference).

facts.why: User profile, chat summary and procedural memory.

blocks.takeaway: Foundry IQ leads for curated, permission-aware content. Custom retrieval wins when you need your own ranking and eval. Memory is for the user, not for the policy library.

items.symptom: Prompt tokens balloon after the tool catalog grows
items.cause: Hundreds of tool definitions travel in every request
items.fix: Turn on tool search (preview). Watch prompt tokens per request to detect it.

items.symptom: A new toolbox version breaks several agents at once
items.cause: Promoting a version to default reaches every consuming agent with no redeploy
items.fix: Test the version first, promote deliberately and keep the previous version to roll back (inference).

items.symptom: The agent cites a document the user may not read
items.cause: The knowledge base ran under a shared identity, or the source has no ACL sync
items.fix: Run under the caller's Entra identity and confirm ACL sync for each source [[r6]].

items.symptom: Delegation to a sibling agent fails after migration
items.cause: The classic Connected Agents tool is not in the new Foundry Agent Service
items.fix: Use the A2A tool, or Microsoft Agent Framework orchestration in hosted code [[r21]].

items.symptom: Memory returns stale or wrong policy answers
items.cause: Memory is per-user and LLM-consolidated, so it is the wrong store for shared documents (inference)
items.fix: Put shared documents in Foundry IQ or file search and keep memory for user facts.

items.title: Go deeper: what a toolbox can and cannot hold

blocks.caption: Toolbox coverage on 2026-10-13
head: In a toolbox
Direct integration only
rows: MCP, web search, Azure AI Search, code interpreter, file search, OpenAPI
A2A, browser automation, Fabric IQ, Work IQ
Grounding with Bing, computer use, image generation
SharePoint, Fabric data agent, Azure Functions

blocks.md: Logic Apps does not appear in the toolbox table, and I could not confirm it as a built-in agent tool on 2026-10-13. Check the page before you promise it.

items.title: Go deeper: tool search and skills (preview)

blocks.md: Tool search hides tools by default and exposes two meta-tools, `tool_search` and `call_tool`, with pin, add-context and auto-pin controls. A toolbox can then hold hundreds of tools without flooding context. **Skills** are versioned, immutable, reusable multi-step workflows delivered through MCP resources. Both work only through a toolbox [[r3]].

items.title: Go deeper: agent to agent after Connected Agents

blocks.md: The classic Connected Agents tool is not available in the new service [[r21]]. The docs name two replacements: the A2A tool, which accepts any A2A endpoint including another Foundry agent exposed as an A2A endpoint, and Workflows. Workflows are preview and retire on 2026-12-01, and the GA page says to use Microsoft Agent Framework for new development [[r11]]. A Foundry agent can also be exposed as an incoming A2A endpoint.

items.title: Go deeper: Foundry IQ and memory

blocks.md:
A Foundry IQ knowledge base holds knowledge sources and retrieval settings and runs on Azure AI Search agentic retrieval [[r6]]. Retrieval reasoning effort is minimal, low or medium. Fabric IQ and Work IQ are sibling workloads. The API is GA by Search REST API version and portal access is preview as of 2026-10-13.

Foundry memory is preview [[r7]]. It extracts, consolidates (an LLM merges and resolves conflicts) and retrieves. The three types are user profile, chat summary and procedural, all on by default. The docs advise retrieving the user profile early and the chat summary per turn.

quiz.q: Select every tool that is direct-integration only and cannot sit inside a toolbox on 2026-10-13.
quiz.explain: Computer use, SharePoint and Azure Functions are direct only, along with Grounding with Bing, image generation, the Fabric data agent and client-side function calling. Azure AI Search and code interpreter are both toolbox tools.

quiz.q: Foundry Workflows (preview) retire on 2026-12-01. How many days remain from 2026-10-13 to the retirement date?
quiz.hint: Count the rest of October, all of November and the first of December.
quiz.explain: October 13 to October 31 is 18 days, November adds 30 and December 1 adds 1, so 49 days. Use that window to move delegation to the A2A tool or Agent Framework orchestration.

quiz.q: After adding many catalog tools, requests carry most of their tokens in tool definitions and answers get worse. What change fits?
options: Lower the temperature so the model is less likely to pick tools it does not need on each turn
Switch every tool to client-side function calling
Raise the Foundry IQ reasoning effort to medium
Turn on tool search (preview) so tools sit behind `tool_search` and `call_tool`
quiz.explain: Tool search hides tools by default and exposes two meta-tools, so definitions stop flooding context. Temperature does not shrink the tool list, client-side calling still sends definitions, and Foundry IQ effort concerns retrieval, not tools.

quiz.q: Which store fits the statement 'prefers metric units and a formal tone, remembered across chats' as of 2026-10-13?
options: Foundry memory, using the user profile type, if the team accepts its preview status
Foundry IQ, because a knowledge base syncs ACLs for every source it connects to and honors Purview labels
File search over whatever documents the user uploaded in the last chat
A toolbox skill, because skills are versioned reusable workflows that persist
quiz.explain: User profile memory holds preferences across sessions and is preview. Foundry IQ serves curated org content, file search serves user documents and skills are workflows delivered through MCP resources, not user facts.

takeaways: A toolbox centralizes auth, guardrails and versions, and a promotion reaches every consumer
Some tools are direct only, so check eligibility before promising one catalog
Connected Agents is gone in the new service, and Workflows retire on 2026-12-01
Foundry IQ is for curated permission-aware content, memory is for the user
